# Know Your Context Bank: Repairing Inconsistency and Measuring Generalization in Context-Aware Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#context-bank)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-24**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.26775v1) · arXiv:2611.26775v1, 19 November 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 27 PDF pages: Sections 1–7; reproducibility, ethics and AI-use statements; references; Appendices A–H; Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–15. Rendered Figure 1 on p.4, Figure 2/Table 13 on p.24 and Table 4 on p.9 visually inspected. No additional linked supplement was identified.

## Research question

Individually defensible question–SQL examples can encode incompatible business conventions, while ordinary accuracy hides how far a model generalizes beyond its context bank.

## Method

Decomposes queries into semantic units grounded in question wording or schema structure and distills align–conflict–novel judgments into a scorer. Conflict flags prioritize review; entry audits and an editable rulebook decide removals. CAT generates questions at scored distances from cleaned banks.

## Evaluation

Uses BIRD, Spider and LiveSQLBench for bank analysis; matched-size BIRD fine-tuning controls, convention-open prompting experiments, and CAT-BIRD/CAT-Spider execution evaluation. The scorer is assessed against constructed and LLM-labeled pairs, with human calibration and a separate expert-audit overlap check.

## What the results support

Cleaned BIRD training improves over a stratified random control across four epochs. Demonstrations matching the gold convention beat opposing examples. Retrieval benefits generally decline with distance; fine-tuning results depend on the dataset, backbone and learning rate.

## Limits and qualifications

Most cleaning removals are per-entry defects, so training gains do not isolate consistency. Conflict scores are not probabilities or verified contradictions. Gold conventions determine matched prompts. LLM-generated tests, imposed baseline difficulty, nearest-neighbor conflict checks, simple retrieval and single seeds constrain transfer; scorer dialect portability remains unverified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Connects underspecification to conflicting reusable context and evaluates context dependence explicitly. It does not establish intrinsic unanswerability, automatic recovery of organizational intent, formal semantic guarantees or a live clarification policy.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cleaning improves fine-tuning by resolving cross-entry inconsistency alone. | Table 2 reports cleaned versus stratified same-size random gains at all four epochs, averaging about 2.6 points. Track A removes 1,252 of the 1,332 removed BIRD-train entries, and Appendix H explicitly leaves a Track-B-only training arm to future work. There is one training seed per arm. | Section 5.1/Table 2, pp.6–7; Appendix D/Table 10, pp.20–21; Appendix H items 4–5, p.27 | Supports the combined cleaning procedure under the tested recipe; it does not isolate consistency as the cause or supply independent seed-level replication. |
| The 92.4% external-audit agreement establishes broad detection accuracy. | Among 1,821 questions shared with BIRD-Platinum, 317 of 343 removed questions had expert SQL corrections, compared with 45.6% of all shared questions. Appendix D says the protocol catches only 33–38% of expert corrections. | Section 4.2, p.6; Appendix D, Agreement with BIRD-Platinum, p.21 | The 92.4% is overlap among removed entries within the shared audited subset, not recall, a global error-prevalence estimate or complete expert validation of the ledger. |
| Consistent examples identify the uniquely correct convention. | Matched and opposite prompts are defined against each question’s existing gold SQL. Both convention choices can be defensible, and BHI scores both equally clean. The 120-question comparison gives a 13.3-point matched-minus-opposite gap; the two 60-question strata have p=.11 and p=.002. | Section 5.2/Table 3, p.7; Appendix E.1–E.3/Table 11, pp.21–22 | Shows steering toward a specified gold convention under controlled prompting; it does not infer user preference or demonstrate that one convention is universally correct. |
| CAT establishes a universal boundary when three quarters of query logic is new. | Distances come from the learned alignment scorer. CAT-BIRD selects questions using no-context performance; conflict checks examine the source and about 18 neighbors. The same two models generate probes and are tested with lexical retrieval. CAT-Spider far groups are not difficulty-matched; its Qwen gains fall below the no-bank control at d3 and dmax. | Section 6/Table 4, pp.8–9; Appendix F/Table 14, pp.24–25; Appendix H item 2, pp.26–27 | Supports a conditional distance-dependent pattern, not an exact semantic novelty threshold or a universal generalization law. Retriever recall, generation style, sample size and fine-tuning recipe remain relevant. |
